summary: An interactive Martian mission game for primary school children to learn by playing a simulation that lets you organise a team and react to emergencies like storms and radiation surges. The aim is to help children become interested in and understand, at a basic level, the challenges of a future Mars mission while developing task management skills, resourcefulness, and having fun. This is important as it helps bring interest and awareness from the younger generation to activities in space as well as some of the concepts that affect them. To this end, we have prioritised accessibility and ease of use so that younger kids who are already adept at other kids' games will have no issues adjusting to our game.
details:
We made the game in Godot because it is a lightweight and easy-to-use game engine, with the intent of being able to optimise and port the game to browsers/phones later on.

The game works as a day-by-day survival game where the objective is to survive 30 days on Mars while performing tasks to save up "research" points to be able to leave the planet. The game ultimately boils down to resource management, balancing power, life support, radiation levels, as well as having decision-making aspects, where random events such as storms, the day/night cycle (and accompanying radiation values taken from NASA databases) will affect how you need to act in the game to survive. We were also planning to add a random mission system where you are able to send some of your astronauts out on EVA in exchange for research and power rewards.
dataRefs: Mars Science Laboratory (MSL), Radiation Assessment Detector (RAD), Level 1 Observational Counter Data
